title: A REQUIREMENT — what must be TRUE for the program's claim to stand
_role: Not 'what could we do' (a route) and not 'what did we run' (a lane), but what has to HOLD. Its job is to bound what may be claimed: read down a requirement's column and THE WEAKEST CELL SETS THE CEILING.
_why_it_did_not_exist_until_2026_08_05: See instrument.schema.json — these two collections were the unschema'd pair, and the untyped `served_by`/`serves` relation between them accumulated eleven disagreements and six prose values before anything noticed.

graph_node.description: Its box in the dependency diagram. `null` is meaningful: a requirement that BOUNDS every node — a scope or submission condition — cannot be drawn as an ordinary box without implying it can be discharged in sequence.

verified_by.description: ⭐ SysML `verify`, and the ONE asserted direction of it. `instrument.verifies` is derived from this and may never be written. ⛔ THE PATTERN IS THE POINT: until 2026-08-05 the reverse edge was also asserted, untyped, and held prose — 'the ATR route's structural precondition', 'the exon-level and residue-level definition of every fusion OBJECT'. A pattern-matched array cannot hold a paraphrase.

verified_by_note.description: The narrative reading of the coverage — including instruments deliberately NOT listed and why. ⚠ It may not be the only place an instrument is named: an instrument described here and absent from `verified_by` is the exact defect that made R13 report 'NO instrument at all' while its own note said one exists and is staged.

coverage_gap.description: ⛔ REQUIRED WHENEVER `verified_by` IS EMPTY AND THE REQUIREMENT IS NOT DEAD, and [Q3] errors when it is missing — omitting it must not be the quiet way to avoid answering. 'Nothing built yet' and 'nothing CAN be built here' license opposite actions, and [Q3] reported them identically until this field existed: R6 is a computable term nobody has computed, while R4's own note reads '⛔ none — needs a bench' against a program CLAUDE.md §5 states has no wet lab, and R16's claim ceiling says the paper's contribution 'is the target's computational druggability/selectivity, not EMC efficacy'. Only `buildable` warns; the other two are stated scope boundaries reported once as INFO. ⚠ A DEAD requirement carries none — the deadness is the answer, and asserting a gap for it would be a second home for that fact.

coverage_gap_why.description: The evidence for the gap classification, in the requirement's own terms. A bare enum with no reason is how a scope boundary becomes unfalsifiable.

claim_ceiling.description: ⛔ What may be claimed from this requirement TODAY. A requirement with no stated ceiling cannot bound what may be claimed from it, which is the register's whole job — [Q2] errors on its absence.

claim_ceiling_raw.description: The roadmap's verbatim wording, stored so the decomposition is LOSSLESS and check_requirement_source_agreement can compare the two without a snapshot.
